title: Soviet invasion of Manchuria (August Storm)
summary: The day after declaring war on Japan on 8 August 1945, about 1.5 million Soviet troops under Marshal Vasilevsky invaded Japanese-held Manchuria. The Kwantung Army collapsed, and an estimated 1.6 to 1.7 million Japanese troops surrendered in the following weeks; Soviet forces also landed on Sakhalin, in northern Korea and in the Kurils.

uncertainty.note: The offensive began on 9 August 1945 and fighting and surrenders continued for weeks; no opened page gave a firm end date. Force sizes and prisoner counts are estimates (the National WWII Museum gives about 1.5 million Soviet troops and 1.6-1.7 million Japanese surrendering).

as_recorded.value: the lightning advance of the Red Army launched on August 9
began the day after the Soviet declaration of war

where.historical_name: Manchuria, held by Japan's Kwantung Army

importance.justification: The offensive destroyed Japan's main continental army, shaped the Japanese surrender, and set the stage for the division of Korea.

audience_note: Describes a large military campaign; sources also report mass rape and pillage against civilians in occupied areas.

beats.caption: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan, honoring its Yalta pledge to enter the war three months after Germany's surrender.
About 1.5 million Soviet troops under Vasilevsky invaded Manchuria the next day.
Roughly 1.6 to 1.7 million Japanese troops surrendered in the weeks after the invasion began.
